newsitem.title: FRANCE: Murdered girl's parents hit out at French police.
newsitem.headline: Murdered girl's parents hit out at French police.

text.p: The parents of a 13-year-old British girl raped and murdered on a school trip to France have demanded that paramilitary gendarmes be dropped from the probe, their lawyer said on Thursday.

Attorney Herve Rouzaud said he had sent a letter to investigating magistrate Gerard Zaug demanding checks on how a first suspect, homeless Frenchman Patrice Pade, had admitted the murder and then been cleared after genetic testing.

"At the parents' request, I have sent the judge a demand for Patrice Pade to be asked about the circumstances of his questioning and to be confronted with the gendarmes who led the probe," Rouzaud said.
"Caroline's parents have reported persistent rumours in Britain that Pade was apparently beaten and that checks on some of his alibis were not properly recorded," he added.

Pade, 39, was detained in July a few days after the body of Caroline was found in a youth hostel in the village of Pleine-Fougeres in Brittany, northwestern France. He was released in August after DNA tests.
Rouzaud said the family reckoned that, if their suspicions about the early handling of the probe were confirmed, then the criminal police might take over the investigation.

Local gendarmerie chief Rene Commer, in charge of the probe, said the accusations were grotesque. "We still have 15 officers working full time on the case. We never had fewer than that. I don't see how another service could do any better."
Dickinson was raped and smothered in her bed in a room she was sharing with four other girls in a youth hostel in the village. She was among 40 children from Launceston Community College in Cornwall.
